name: Art trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about visual art: painters, sculptors, famous works, movements, techniques, museums. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
items.explain: The Mona Lisa is an oil painting by Leonardo da Vinci, made between about 1503 and 1519.

items.question: In which Paris museum does the Mona Lisa hang?
items.explain: The Mona Lisa hangs behind bulletproof glass in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

items.question: What type of painting is the Mona Lisa?
items.explain: The Mona Lisa is a half-length portrait of a seated woman.

items.question: Which technique of soft, smoky shading gives the Mona Lisa's face its hazy look?
items.explain: Leonardo used sfumato, a subtle blending of light and shadow, to give the face its soft, lifelike look.

items.question: Which French ruler once had the Mona Lisa hung in his bedroom in the Tuileries Palace?
items.explain: Napoleon borrowed the painting for his bedroom for about four years. It went back on show in the Louvre in 1804.

items.question: Who painted The Starry Night in 1889?
items.explain: The Starry Night is an oil painting that Vincent van Gogh made at Saint-Rémy in June 1889.

source.title: Vincent van Gogh. The Starry Night. Saint Rémy, June 1889

items.question: Which New York City museum holds Van Gogh's The Starry Night?
items.explain: The Museum of Modern Art acquired The Starry Night in 1941, and it has been a visitor favorite there ever since.

source.title: Virtual Views: Van Gogh's Starry Night

items.question: In which country did Van Gogh paint The Starry Night during a stay at a mental hospital?
items.explain: He painted it at a mental hospital in Saint-Rémy, in the south of France.

source.title: MoMA: Shedding light on The Starry Night

items.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
items.explain: In 1508 Pope Julius II gave the job to Michelangelo, who painted the ceiling and finished it in 1512.

items.question: The Sistine Chapel, with its famous Michelangelo ceiling, lies within which state?
items.explain: The Sistine Chapel is a papal chapel built within the Vatican and is part of the Vatican Museums.

items.question: Which painting technique, using pigment on wet plaster, did Michelangelo use for the Sistine Chapel ceiling?
items.explain: The ceiling is a fresco, painted in pigment on wet plaster.

source.title: Michelangelo, Ceiling of the Sistine Chapel

items.question: The nine central panels of the Sistine Chapel ceiling show stories from which book of the Bible?
items.explain: The central panels show scenes from the Book of Genesis, ending with the Creation at the altar end.

source.title: The Sistine Chapel's vault by Michelangelo

items.question: About how long did Michelangelo take to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling?
items.explain: He worked on the ceiling from 1508 to 1512, so the job took about four years.

source.title: Michelangelo, Ceiling of the Sistine Chapel

items.question: Who painted the anti-war mural Guernica in 1937?
items.explain: Guernica is a large oil painting by Pablo Picasso, made after the German bombing of the Spanish town of Guernica.

items.question: Picasso's Guernica responds to a bombing that took place during which conflict?
items.explain: The 1937 bombing of the Basque town took place during the Spanish Civil War, and the painting drew worldwide attention to that war.

items.question: Which colors did Picasso use for Guernica?
items.explain: Picasso painted Guernica in a stark palette of gray, black and white.

items.question: Pablo Picasso, who painted Guernica, was an artist from which country?
items.explain: Guernica is described as a work by the Spanish artist Pablo Picasso.

items.question: Which art movement took its name from Monet's painting Impression, Sunrise?
items.explain: A critic mocked the painting's title in 1874 and the term Impressionism stuck as the movement's name.

items.question: In which city was Monet's Impression, Sunrise first shown, at an independent exhibition in 1874?
items.explain: It was first shown in Paris at an independent exhibition that offered an alternative to the official Salon.

items.question: Monet's Impression, Sunrise shows the harbor of which French port?
items.explain: The painting shows the port of Le Havre at sunrise, with small rowboats in the foreground.

items.question: Who painted The Persistence of Memory, famous for its melting clocks?
items.explain: The Persistence of Memory is an oil painting made by Salvador Dalí in 1931.

source.title: Salvador Dalí. The Persistence of Memory. 1931

items.question: What everyday objects appear to melt in Dalí's The Persistence of Memory?
items.explain: The painting is known for its soft, melting clocks spread across a desolate landscape.

source.title: The Persistence of Memory (1931) by Salvador Dali

items.question: Dalí's The Persistence of Memory is a classic work of which art movement?
items.explain: MoMA describes the painting's aim as the classic Surrealist ambition of discrediting the world of reality.

source.title: Salvador Dalí. The Persistence of Memory. 1931

items.question: What famous feature is missing from the ancient statue known as the Venus de Milo?
items.explain: The marble statue of the goddess stands in the Louvre and is famous for its missing arms.

items.question: Which goddess is the Venus de Milo commonly thought to represent?
items.explain: The statue is commonly thought to represent Aphrodite, the Greek goddess of love and beauty, whom the Romans identified with Venus.

items.question: What material is the Venus de Milo carved from?
items.explain: The Venus de Milo is an ancient marble sculpture.

items.question: Which ancient civilization made the Venus de Milo?
items.explain: The Venus de Milo is an ancient Greek marble statue of Aphrodite, found on the island of Melos in 1820.

items.question: Who sculpted the 17-foot marble statue of David that stands in Florence?
items.explain: Michelangelo carved the marble David between 1501 and 1504.

items.question: The original of Michelangelo's David stands in a gallery in which Italian city?
items.explain: The original David is in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Florence.

items.question: What weapon does Michelangelo's David carry over his shoulder?
items.explain: The statue shows the biblical hero nude with a slingshot over his shoulder, just before he faces Goliath.

items.question: Which artist created The Scream?
items.explain: Edvard Munch first created The Scream in 1893 and then made several versions of it.

items.question: Edvard Munch, creator of The Scream, was an artist from which country?
items.explain: Munch was a Norwegian artist, and the work was conceived in Kristiania, now Oslo.

items.question: Munch's work, including The Scream, strongly influenced which art movement?
items.explain: Munch's work, including The Scream, had a formative influence on the Expressionist movement.

items.question: Who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring?
items.explain: Girl with a Pearl Earring is Vermeer's most famous painting.

source.title: Johannes Vermeer Girl with a Pearl Earring

items.question: Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring has been given which nickname?
items.explain: Smarthistory notes that this enigmatic character study was dubbed the "Dutch Mona Lisa".

source.title: Johannes Vermeer, Girl with a Pearl Earring

items.question: Johannes Vermeer was a painter from which country?
items.explain: Vermeer was a Dutch artist who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring around 1665.

items.question: Which artist painted the series Campbell's Soup Cans in 1961–62?
items.explain: Campbell's Soup Cans is a series of 32 paintings that Andy Warhol produced between 1961 and 1962.

items.question: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans are a canonical symbol of which art movement?
items.explain: The series is widely regarded as a canonical symbol of Pop art.

items.question: Andy Warhol, creator of Campbell's Soup Cans, was an artist of which nationality?
items.explain: Warhol was an American artist who moved to New York City in 1949.

items.question: Who sculpted The Thinker, the pensive seated nude male figure?
items.explain: The Thinker is one of the best-known sculptures by the French artist Auguste Rodin.

items.question: Rodin's The Thinker is best known as a cast sculpture in which metal?
items.explain: The Thinker is a bronze sculpture, and many casts exist in a variety of sizes.

items.question: Who painted The Birth of Venus?
items.explain: The Birth of Venus is a Renaissance painting by Sandro Botticelli from the 1480s.

source.title: The Birth of Venus, 1483 - 1485 - Sandro Botticelli - WikiArt.org

items.question: Botticelli's The Birth of Venus hangs in which gallery?
items.explain: The painting is in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence.

source.title: The Birth of Venus, 1483 - 1485 - Sandro Botticelli - WikiArt.org

items.question: In Botticelli's The Birth of Venus, what is the goddess standing on?
items.explain: The newly born Venus stands nude in a giant scallop shell.

source.title: The Birth of Venus, 1483 - 1485 - Sandro Botticelli - WikiArt.org

items.question: Frida Kahlo is best known for painting what kind of artworks?
items.explain: Kahlo is best known for her brilliantly colored self-portraits that deal with identity, the human body and death.

items.question: Frida Kahlo was a painter from which country?
items.explain: Kahlo was a Mexican painter, born in Coyoacán in 1907.

items.question: Which Mexican muralist did Frida Kahlo marry in 1929?
items.explain: In 1929 Kahlo married the much older Mexican muralist Diego Rivera.

items.question: Who painted The Last Supper on a wall in Milan?
items.explain: Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper from about 1495 to 1498 for Duke Ludovico Sforza.

items.question: In which Italian city is Leonardo's Last Supper, in a convent dining hall?
items.explain: It covers an end wall of the dining hall of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan.

items.question: What does Jesus announce in Leonardo's Last Supper that sparks the apostles' reactions?
answers: One of them will betray him
One of them will become king
One of them will leave Judea
One of them will build a temple
items.correct: One of them will betray him
items.explain: The painting shows each apostle's reaction to Jesus saying that one of them would betray him.
